analyzed_vuln.description: `mrb_hash_set()` replaces a mutable String key with a newly allocated frozen duplicate via `h_key_for()`, but does not GC-protect that duplicate before calling `h_set()`. `h_set()` can execute arbitrary Ruby code while hashing keys (notably when `ar_set()` converts a full array-form hash to indexed-table form and `ib_init()` invokes an existing object's `hash` method). A reentrant full GC can therefore collect the not-yet-published duplicate before the post-insertion write barrier. Subsequent `ht_set()` hashes the dangling String and `mrb_byte_hash_step()` reads its freed backing buffer, causing the observed heap-use-after-free.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Ruby input must construct an array-form Hash at `AR_MAX_SIZE` entries, including a non-primitive key whose overridden `hash` method can trigger GC, then insert a mutable, non-embedded String as the capacity-crossing new key. `mrb_hash_set()` duplicates/freezes that String; AR-to-HT conversion hashes the earlier callback-bearing key, whose callback runs a full GC while the duplicate is reachable only from an unprotected C local and not yet stored in the Hash. GC frees the duplicate/String buffer, after which insertion hashes the stale key and crashes in `mrb_byte_hash_step()`.

args: In mruby/src/hash.c, what is the appropriate existing GC-rooting idiom for a newly allocated mrb_value that must survive a call capable of arbitrary Ruby callbacks? Specifically assess adding mrb_gc_protect(mrb, key) between h_key_for() and h_set() in mrb_hash_set(), including arena lifetime/growth concerns and whether an arena save/restore should be used.

The reported UAF is in mruby/src/hash.c:mrb_hash_set: h_key_for duplicates and freezes a mutable String key, then h_set may invoke Ruby hash callbacks during array-to-index conversion before publishing the duplicate into the hash. A full GC collects the duplicate held only in a C local. The obvious root fix is mrb_gc_protect(mrb, key) before h_set. I have observed mrb_hash_shift uses mrb_gc_protect on values removed from the hash before allocating an association. I need to preserve API behavior and avoid unnecessary arena leaks while ensuring the duplicate remains rooted through h_set and write barriers.
